Settings.RootFolderNameHint: Journal folder that holds imported notes.
Settings.ShowBacklinksHint: List the notes that link to a note at the bottom of the GM view.
Settings.AutocompleteHint: Type [[ in a Codex note to link notes, actors, items, spells, monsters and more; [[/ for roll buttons.
Settings.FontSizeHint: Size of body text in Codex notes, on this computer.
Settings.InlineEditHint: Foundry's edit control opens the Codex editor right where you are reading, instead of a separate window at the top of the note. The window still opens when the note isn't on screen.
Settings.DblclickEditHint: Double-click a paragraph, list item or callout in a Codex note to edit it right there.
Settings.CitationPrefixesHint: Inline code starting with one of these (comma separated) shows as a small book reference instead of code, e.g. `PHB, Ch. 7 › Fireball`. A prefix containing a backslash is read as a regular expression.

Import.Title: Import Obsidian vault
Import.Intro: Pick your vault folder. Notes become journal entries with Markdown pages in the Codex folder. The files stay where they are; nothing is uploaded except images that notes embed.
Import.FoldersHint: Unticked folders are skipped. Sources, Tools and editor folders are off by default.
Import.Conflicts: A note changed in both the vault and Foundry
Import.ConflictVault: Take the vault version (Foundry edits are lost)
Import.ConflictMadeCopy: saved the vault version as a copy

Report.Title: Codex import report
Report.Dangling: Links to notes that don't exist
Report.Ambiguous: Links that matched more than one note

Export.Title: Export notes to the vault
Export.Intro: Saves notes as Markdown with the vault's folder layout. Unzip over the vault folder to update it. Links to world actors, items and scenes are written as [[actor:Name]] so they survive a re-import.
Export.OnlyChanged: Only notes changed since import or last export
Export.MarkSynced: Mark exported notes as in sync with the vault
Export.NoFolderAccess: Writing straight into a folder needs a secure connection (https or localhost); the zip works everywhere.
